## 90-Day Project Coordinator Transition Plan for Dublin

You already have a strong base for project coordination: 4 years in administration, solid Excel capability, and a clear move toward project management. The plan below focuses on turning that experience into credible project delivery skills while keeping your salary target and 2-year progression goal in view.

## 90-Day Roadmap and Skill-Building Priorities

### 90-Day Transition Plan
| Phase | Timeframe | Main Goal | Key Actions | Output |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| 1. Positioning | Days 1-30 | Reframe admin experience as coordination experience | Map your duties to scheduling, tracking, reporting, stakeholder support; update CV/LinkedIn; create a skills gap list; start applying to project coordinator roles in Dublin | Targeted CV, LinkedIn refresh, role shortlist |
| 2. Capability Build | Days 31-60 | Add practical project delivery skills | Learn Agile fundamentals; practice status reporting, RAID logs, meeting minutes, action tracking; build one Excel dashboard or tracker for a sample project | Project toolkit, interview stories, sample tracker |
| 3. Credibility + Applications | Days 61-90 | Show readiness for a coordinator role | Apply consistently; tailor cover letters; prepare STAR examples; network with PMs/coordinators; practice salary conversations around €42k–€48k | Interview pipeline, refined pitch, negotiation script |

### Top Skills to Build First
| Skill | Why it matters | Priority | How to build it fast |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Project coordination basics | Core of the role: timelines, actions, follow-ups, dependencies | High | Learn project lifecycle, meeting cadence, action logs, status updates |
| Agile fundamentals | Many Dublin teams expect working knowledge even for non-PM roles | High | Understand Scrum roles, ceremonies, sprint planning, retrospectives |
| Stakeholder communication | Keeps work moving across teams and levels | High | Practice concise updates, escalation notes, and meeting summaries |
| Excel for reporting | Turns raw data into useful project tracking | High | Build trackers, dashboards, formulas, pivots, conditional formatting |
| Risk and issue tracking | Helps you support delivery proactively | Medium | Learn RAID logs and simple mitigation language |
| Prioritisation and time management | Essential for juggling admin, deadlines, and project tasks | Medium | Use weekly planning, task triage, and dependency tracking |
| Basic project tools | Common in coordinator roles | Medium | Get comfortable with Jira, Trello, Asana, MS Project, or Monday.com |

### 90-Day Weekly Focus
| Weeks | Focus | What to Practice | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1-2 | Role translation | Rewrite admin achievements in project language | Stronger CV language |
| 3-4 | Excel and reporting | Track tasks, deadlines, and progress in a clean dashboard | Interview-ready work sample |
| 5-6 | Agile basics | Learn ceremonies, artefacts, and team roles | Explain Agile clearly in interviews |
| 7-8 | Stakeholder management | Draft updates, escalation notes, and meeting minutes | Better communication examples |
| 9-10 | Job applications | Tailor CV and cover letter for each role | More interviews |
| 11-12 | Interview prep | STAR stories, salary discussion, transition narrative | Confident interviewing |

## Resume Summary Tailored to Your Goal

**Resume Summary**
Organised and detail-focused administrative professional with 4 years of experience supporting busy teams through scheduling, reporting, documentation, and stakeholder coordination. Strong Excel skills and a practical approach to process improvement, task tracking, and cross-team communication. Currently transitioning into project coordination, with growing knowledge of Agile delivery methods and a clear goal of progressing into project management within 2 years. Based in Dublin and targeting project coordinator roles in the €42,000–€48,000 range.
